system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: production cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) at work
G2: production on-call
G3: cluster administration
G4: CKA certification (not yet passed)
G5: Terraform at work

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing CKA or Terraform Associate as held certifications
T2: Claiming AWS/GCP production experience or 'managed Kubernetes clusters'
T3: Presenting homelab tools (Argo CD, Prometheus, Terraform) as work experience
T4: Claiming production on-call / SRE incident ownership
T5: Retitling her current job as 'DevOps Engineer' instead of her real title
T6: Old cover letter is addressed to her current employer and says she is at Brightmill

# OUTPUT 1: CV
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer | DevOps and Platform Engineering
marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including a recent focus on CI/CD pipelines, test
environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and has built
Helm-based ephemeral environments on a shared Kubernetes cluster. Personal experience includes a
k3s homelab with GitOps, monitoring and Terraform-provisioned VPS infrastructure. Seeking to move
into a DevOps or platform engineering role.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, pipeline optimization, artifact publishing
Containers and orchestration: Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access
and test-environment deployments), k3s
Infrastructure as Code and GitOps: Terraform (personal VPS project), Argo CD, Ansible (basic)
Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki; test metrics dashboards
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)
Languages and data: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, PostgreSQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems: Linux, Git
SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health Software | 2023–2024
• Built a GitLab CI workflow that deploys a short-lived application and PostgreSQL environment
with seeded data to the shared Kubernetes cluster using Helm.
• Configured automatic environment cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity; QA and product
teams use the environments for feature review and e2e testing.
• Technologies: GitLab CI, Helm, Kubernetes, Docker, Bash, PostgreSQL.
CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health Software | 2022
• Profiled pipelines for three teams, parallelized test jobs, added dependency caching and separated
e2e tests into their own stage.
• Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner cost by about 30%.
• Technologies: GitLab CI, Docker, pytest-xdist.
Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health Software | 2023
• Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team.
• Helped teams identify and address frequent offenders; the flaky test rate fell from 7% to below 1%.
• Technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, Grafana, GitLab API.
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
• Set up a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster with applications deployed from a Git repository
using Argo CD.
• Added Prometheus, Grafana and Loki monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
• Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform.
• Technologies: k3s, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Terraform, Ansible (basic).
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software | 2021–Present
• Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering builds,
unit, integration and e2e test stages, and artifact publishing.
• Built ephemeral test environments for merge requests using Docker Compose and later Helm charts
on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster.
• Maintain a pytest and Playwright e2e suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky rate from
7% to below 1%.
• Wrote Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding.
• Wrote the internal guide to how CI works, now used in team onboarding.
• Mentored two QA interns in 2023.
QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | 2019–2021
• Tested web and mobile applications through manual and automated testing for client projects.
• Introduced a Selenium and Java automated regression suite for the largest client project.
• Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.
Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
• Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.
EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATIONS
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam booked for January 2027 (not yet
certified)
LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role.
My work has increasingly focused on the infrastructure around software delivery: CI pipelines,
Kubernetes-based test environments, and tools that make changes easier to validate and
operate. Corvale’s work connecting a new train fleet with cloud services is an opportunity to
apply that experience to a platform with a clear operational purpose.
At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines used by three product teams and built
merge-request environments deployed with Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster. I also
improved pipeline performance from 38 to 14 minutes, with monthly CI runner costs down
about 30%, and created Grafana dashboards that helped teams reduce flaky tests from 7% to
below 1%. These projects have involved working across teams and documenting how the CI
system works for onboarding.
I have also built a personal three-node k3s homelab with Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana,
Loki, Traefik and cert-manager, and used Terraform to provision infrastructure for a small
Hetzner VPS. My Terraform and cloud experience is currently personal rather than
production-based; my work Kubernetes access is namespace-level, and the platform team
operates the shared cluster. I am preparing for the CKA exam, which is booked for January
2027.
I would bring a practical delivery and automation perspective, experience improving reliability
and observability, and a clear understanding of the limits of my current infrastructure scope. I
would welcome the opportunity to discuss how that background could contribute to Corvale’s
fleet-connectivity platform.
Sincerely,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
